info.title: RevKeen API
info.description:
RevKeen is a fintech-grade API for payments, subscriptions, invoices, and billing. The canonical production MCP server is available at `https://mcp.revkeen.com/mcp`.

**API Version:** `2026-05-01` — Pin with the `RevKeen-Version` header.

**Quick Links:** [Full Documentation](https://docs.revkeen.com) | [Authentication](https://docs.revkeen.com/authentication) | [OAuth](https://docs.revkeen.com/oauth) | [SDKs](https://docs.revkeen.com/sdks) | [Webhooks](#webhooks) | [MCP Guide](https://docs.revkeen.com/mcp)

## Authentication

Two authentication methods are supported:

### API Keys (recommended for server-to-server REST API integrations)

Send your merchant API key in the `x-api-key` header, or as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` — both are accepted. Create and manage keys in the [Dashboard](https://app.revkeen.com/dashboard/settings/general?tab=developer). Use `rk_sandbox_*` for staging/test and `rk_live_*` for production. Keys are scoped, rollable, IP-lockable and revocable; the raw secret is shown once, at creation.

### OAuth 2.1 (recommended for MCP and third-party integrations)

Use OAuth 2.1 with PKCE for authorization code flow or client credentials for server-to-server. Access tokens are opaque, prefixed `rkoa_`, and sent via `Authorization: Bearer rkoa_*`. See the [OAuth guide](https://docs.revkeen.com/oauth) for setup.

- **Authorization Code + PKCE** — user-facing integrations, MCP hosts
- **Client Credentials** — server-to-server, automated workflows
- **Dynamic Client Registration** — MCP hosts that auto-register

## MCP Integration

RevKeen's canonical production MCP server is `https://mcp.revkeen.com/mcp` using Streamable HTTP and OAuth 2.1 bearer tokens.

- **Customer launch surface** — read-first customer v1 tools with least-privilege scopes
- **Host setup guide** — see the [MCP guide](https://docs.revkeen.com/mcp) for ChatGPT, Claude, and compatible MCP hosts

## API Key Scopes

Scopes follow `{resource}:{action}` format (e.g., `invoices:read`, `customers:*`). See [full scope reference](https://docs.revkeen.com/authentication#scopes).

| Category | Scope | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| **Payments & Checkout** | `checkout:read` | View checkout session details |
|  | `checkout:write` | Create and manage checkout sessions |
|  | `cart:read` | View cart session details |
|  | `cart:write` | Create and mutate cart sessions, line items, add-ons |
|  | `payment_links:read` | View payment links |
|  | `payment_links:write` | Create and manage payment links |
|  | `charges:read` | View one-time charges |
|  | `charges:write` | Create one-time charges for customers |
|  | `payments:read` | View payment details |
|  | `payments:write` | Capture or void payments |
|  | `payment_intents:read` | View payment intent details |
|  | `payment_intents:write` | Create, confirm, capture, and cancel payment intents |
|  | `setup_intents:read` | View setup intent details |
|  | `setup_intents:write` | Create, confirm, and cancel setup intents |
|  | `payment_methods:read` | View saved payment methods |
|  | `payment_methods:write` | Attach and detach payment methods |
| **Billing** | `invoices:read` | View invoices |
|  | `invoices:write` | Create, update, and manage invoices |
|  | `subscriptions:read` | View subscriptions |
|  | `subscriptions:write` | Create, update, pause, and cancel subscriptions |
|  | `subscription_schedules:read` | View subscription schedule details |
|  | `subscription_schedules:write` | Create, update, cancel, and release subscription schedules |
|  | `orders:read` | View orders |
|  | `orders:write` | Create and manage orders |
|  | `credit_notes:read` | View credit notes |
|  | `credit_notes:write` | Create and void credit notes |
| **Products & Pricing** | `products:read` | View product catalog |
|  | `products:write` | Create and update products |
|  | `prices:read` | View pricing information |
|  | `prices:write` | Create and update prices |
|  | `discounts:read` | View discount codes |
|  | `discounts:write` | Create and manage discount codes |
|  | `tax_rates:read` | View tax rate configurations |
|  | `tax_rates:write` | Configure tax rates |
| **Usage & Metering** | `meters:read` | View meter configurations |
|  | `meters:write` | Create and update meters |
|  | `usage:read` | View usage events and balances |
|  | `usage:write` | Ingest usage events |
| **Customers** | `customers:read` | View customer information |
|  | `customers:write` | Create and update customers |
|  | `entitlements:read` | View customer entitlements / feature access |
|  | `entitlements:write` | Grant and revoke customer entitlements |
|  | `businesses:read` | View business entities |
|  | `businesses:write` | Manage business entities |
| **Money Movement** | `refunds:read` | View refund details |
|  | `refunds:write` | Issue refunds |
|  | `voids:read` | View voided transactions |
|  | `voids:write` | Void unsettled transactions |
|  | `disputes:read` | View chargebacks and disputes |
|  | `disputes:write` | Respond to disputes |
|  | `payouts:read` | View payout and settlement data |
| **Direct Debit** | `mandates:read` | View Direct Debit mandates and collection status |
|  | `mandates:write` | Create, suspend, reinstate, and cancel Direct Debit mandates |
| **Terminal** | `terminal:read` | View terminal devices and card-present payments |
|  | `terminal:write` | Initiate, cancel, refund, and void terminal payments |
| **Data Exchange** | `exports:read` | View and download data exports |
|  | `exports:write` | Create data exports |
|  | `imports:read` | View import status and history |
|  | `imports:write` | Upload and run data imports |
| **Analytics & Reporting** | `analytics:read` | View analytics and reports |
|  | `finance:read` | View financial reports |
| **Communication** | `comms:read` | View SMS and email delivery logs |
|  | `comms:write` | Send SMS, email, and WhatsApp messages |
|  | `automations:read` | View automations, runs, approvals, and traces |
|  | `automations:write` | Create automations and trigger runs |
| **Integrations** | `apps:read` | View connected applications |
|  | `apps:write` | Manage app connections |
|  | `webhooks:read` | View webhook endpoints |
|  | `webhooks:write` | Manage webhook endpoints |
|  | `integrations:read` | View integration status and sync logs |
|  | `integrations:write` | Activate, configure, and sync integrations |
|  | `events:read` | View webhook event logs |
|  | `events:write` | Resend and test webhook events |
|  | `sync:read` | View sync watermarks and state |
|  | `sync:write` | Update sync watermarks |

## Errors

Every non-2xx response uses one envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", ... } }`. Branch on `error.type` and `error.code`; treat `error.message` as display text only. Error bodies never echo the credential you presented.

| Status | `error.type` | Notes |
|--------|--------------|-------|
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` | Schema validation failed. `details.fields` maps each rejected parameter to its reasons. |
| `401` | `authentication_error` | Missing, invalid, expired or revoked credential. Always carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="revkeen-api"`. |
| `402` | `card_error` | Declined by the issuer or processor; see `decline_code`. |
| `403` | `authorization_error` | The caller is identified but the action is denied — scope, IP allowlist, origin, or merchant mismatch. |
| `409` | `invalid_request_error` or `idempotency_error` | Resource-state conflict, or an `Idempotency-Key` replayed with a different body. |
| `429` | `rate_limit_error` | See Rate Limits below. |
| `500` | `api_error` | Retry with exponential backoff, quoting `error.request_id`. |

`401` codes: `authentication_failed`, `invalid_api_key`, `expired_api_key`, `api_key_revoked`, `session_invalid`, `merchant_required`.

`403` codes: `insufficient_permissions`, `forbidden`, `ip_not_allowed`, `tenant_scope_mismatch`, `no_organization`, `no_merchant`, `merchant_mismatch`, `cart_disabled`, `origin_not_allowed`, `verification_required`, `read_only_impersonation_blocked`, `publishable_key_restricted`, `internal_only`.

## Environments

| Environment | Base URL | API Key Prefix |
|-------------|----------|----------------|
| **Staging** | `https://staging-api.revkeen.com/v2` | `rk_sandbox_*` |
| **Production** | `https://api.revkeen.com/v2` | `rk_live_*` |

## Idempotency

Include `Idempotency-Key` header (UUID) on mutation requests. Keys are valid for 24 hours.

## Rate Limits

| Plan | Requests/min | Burst |
|------|-------------|-------|
| **Staging** | 100 | 200 |
| **Production** | 1000 | 2000 |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Custom |

A rate-limited request returns `429` with `type: rate_limit_error`, `code: rate_limit_exceeded` and `details.retry_after` in whole seconds.

| Header | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `Retry-After` | Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Present on every `429`. |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Requests permitted in the current window, when the limiter publishes one. |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current window. |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | UNIX timestamp in **seconds** at which the window resets. |

post.description: Sent when a payment is successfully captured. **Action required:** Provision goods or services to your customer.
Sent when a payment attempt fails. Contains failure reason and suggested next steps.

object.failure_message: Your card was declined. Please try a different payment method.

post.description: Sent when a new invoice is created, either manually or from a subscription renewal.
Sent when an invoice is fully paid. **Action required:** Fulfill the order or activate the subscription.
Sent when an invoice becomes overdue. Consider sending payment reminders.
Sent when a new subscription is created (before activation).
Sent when a subscription becomes active after successful payment. **Action required:** Grant access to your service.
Sent when a subscription is canceled. Access continues until the end of the billing period.
Sent when a subscription successfully renews. A new invoice has been created and paid.
Sent when a new customer is created.
Sent when customer information is updated.
Sent when a refund is initiated.
Sent when a refund is successfully processed by the payment gateway.
Sent when a void is initiated for an unsettled transaction.
Sent when a void is successfully processed by the payment gateway. The original transaction has been canceled.
Sent when a void fails (e.g., transaction already settled). Consider using a refund instead.

object.failure_reason: Transaction already settled. Use a refund instead.

post.description: Sent when a credit note is created for an invoice.
Sent when a credit note is issued (finalized) and its PDF is generated.
Sent when a credit note is voided (accounting reversal).
Sent when a checkout session is successfully completed. **Action required:** Fulfill the customer's order.
Sent when a checkout session expires before completion.
Sent when a new order is created.
Sent when an order is fully paid. **Action required:** Begin fulfillment.
Sent when a card-present payment is dispatched to a terminal device. The payment is in-progress and awaiting terminal response.
Sent when a card-present payment is approved by the terminal. **Action required:** Provide goods or services to the customer.
Sent when a card-present payment is declined by the terminal or card issuer.
Sent when a card-present payment is cancelled by the merchant before terminal response.
Sent when a card-present payment fails due to timeout, terminal error, or connection loss. Check `failure_reason` field: `timeout`, `terminal_error`, or `connection_lost`.

object.failure_message: Terminal did not respond within 60 seconds

post.description: Sent when a card-present refund is approved by the terminal.
Sent when a card-present void is approved by the terminal. The original transaction has been reversed.
Sent when an order is marked as fulfilled.
Sent when a customer's usage crosses a configured threshold percentage on a meter. Use this to alert customers approaching or exceeding their included allowance.
Sent when a billing period is finalized with final usage quantities. An invoice will be generated shortly after.
Sent when finalized usage records are converted into an invoice for a customer subscription.
Sent after a usage event is accepted by ingestion. This is a high-volume event and should be subscribed to explicitly with narrow endpoint filters.
Sent when a usage event is rejected during ingestion validation. Rejected events are not billable.

object.rejection_message: Property 'quantity' must be a positive number

post.description: Sent when a usage event is considered by a meter but excluded by filter conditions. The event is not billable. Delivery is at-least-once; dedupe on `data.dedupeKey`.
Sent when a usage event cannot be matched to a single active meter (unmatched, ambiguous, or terminal processing failure). Delivery is at-least-once; dedupe on `data.dedupeKey`.
Sent when a hard usage cap refuses the event. The ingest transaction rolled back: nothing was persisted and nothing was charged. Delivery is at-least-once; dedupe on `data.dedupeKey`.
Sent when a usage meter is created.
Sent when a usage meter is updated. The payload includes changed attributes when available.
Sent when a usage meter is archived and can no longer be attached to new pricing.
Sent when a meter price is created for a product price.
Sent when a meter price is updated. The payload includes changed attributes when available.
Sent when a meter price is deactivated and no longer available for new subscriptions.
Sent when a customer signs a Direct Debit mandate instruction. The mandate is pending lodgement with the bank (AUDDIS) — wait for `mandate.activated` before collecting.
Sent when a Direct Debit mandate is created and submitted to Bacs for lodgement. The mandate is not yet collectable — wait for `mandate.activated`.
Sent when a mandate is lodged and active. **Action required:** You can now collect from this customer via Direct Debit.
Sent when the customer's bank rejects the mandate setup (AUDDIS). **Action required:** The mandate cannot be used — re-collect bank details or use another payment method.

object.failure_message: The bank rejected the Direct Debit instruction.

post.description: Sent when a mandate is suspended and can no longer be collected against until reinstated.
Sent when a mandate is cancelled (by you, the customer, or the bank). It can no longer be collected against.
Sent when a Direct Debit collection is scheduled against an active mandate. Includes the working-day collection date.
Sent when the mandatory advance notice for an upcoming collection has been issued to the customer.
Sent when a Direct Debit collection is successfully taken. **Action required:** Provision goods or services to your customer.
Sent when a Direct Debit collection fails (e.g. insufficient funds). Contains the Bacs reason code. **Action required:** RevKeen Recovery may retry or fall back to a stored card per your policy.

object.failure_message: The collection was returned by the customer's bank.

post.description: Sent when a customer raises a Direct Debit indemnity claim (the Bacs chargeback equivalent) and the collection is reversed. **Action required:** Review the disputed collection.
Sent when collected Direct Debit funds are settled and a payout is created. Gross settlement — the bureau fee is reported separately and never netted from the payout.

apiKey.description: Your RevKeen merchant API key. Create and manage keys in [Dashboard → Settings → Developer](https://app.revkeen.com/dashboard/settings/general?tab=developer). Use `rk_sandbox_*` for staging/test and `rk_live_*` for production. The same key may be sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` if that suits your HTTP client better. A missing, invalid, expired, or revoked key returns `401` with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge; a valid key without the required scope returns `403`.

created.description: Unix timestamp when the event was created

livemode.description: Whether this event occurred in live mode

SuccessResponse.description: Generic success confirmation for operations that do not return a resource.

reminder_eligible_now.description: Count of invoices that would match the default overdue ladder (day 1+) at the next hourly reminder cron. With anchor = NOW() on mark, this is typically 0 — the first reminder fires tomorrow.

reminder_eligible_within_7_days.description: Count of invoices that will receive at least one reminder within 7 days of this attestation, assuming the default ladder [1, 7, 14, 30].

InvoiceCommentListDetailResponse.description: A list of invoice comments with extended author details.

InvoiceCommentDetail.description: An invoice comment with extended author details including name, email, and avatar.

InvoiceCommentDetailResponse.description: A single invoice comment with extended author details.

ExternalUpsertResponse.description: Response from an external system upsert, indicating whether the invoice was created or updated along with any warnings.

StaleUpdateResponse.description: Returned when an external upsert is skipped because the incoming timestamp is older than the stored version.

UnchangedContentResponse.description: Returned when an external upsert is skipped because the substantive content hash matched the stored row — no DB write performed.

MeterPriceError.description: Error response returned when a meter price operation fails.

pricing_model.description: Pricing model. 'percentage' charges a basis-points percentage of the metered amount (REV-3465); other models charge per unit, graduated tiers, volume tiers, or packages.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. A usage-based subscription has one currency; metered events attributed to it are assumed to be in this currency and are not FX-converted by RevKeen.

unit_amount_minor.description: Price per unit in minor units (for per_unit). For a sub-penny rate use `unit_amount_decimal`.

unit_amount_decimal.description: Exact per-unit rate in minor units as a decimal string (sub-penny safe, e.g. "0.02" = 0.02 pence). Takes precedence over `unit_amount_minor`. Mirrors Stripe's `unit_amount_decimal`.

flat_fee_minor.description: Base charge per period in minor units

cost_per_unit_minor.description: Merchant's cost per unit for margin intelligence

filter_conditions.description: Optional event property predicates for dimensional pricing. Empty or omitted = base/fallthrough price.

filter_priority.description: Tie-breaker when multiple matching filters have the same specificity.

pay_in_advance.description: When true, matching usage events debit the customer's prepaid wallet at ingest time.

spending_minimum_cents.description: Minimum minor-unit amount applied to each pay-in-advance usage drawdown.

percentage_rate_bps.description: Rate in basis points. 70 = 0.7%. Required when pricing_model='percentage'. Range 0–10000 (0%–100%).

CreateMeterPriceRequest.description: Parameters for creating a price attached to a usage meter, defining per-unit cost, tiered tiers, or a percentage rate.

up_to.description: Upper bound of this tier (1-based inclusive). null = open-ended final tier. New clients should use this canonical shape; legacy first_unit/last_unit is accepted during the deprecation window.

unit_amount_minor.description: Per-unit price in this tier (minor units). For a sub-penny per-tier rate use `unit_amount_decimal`. Optional when `unit_amount_decimal` or `flat_amount_minor` is supplied.

unit_amount_decimal.description: Exact per-unit rate for this tier in minor units as a decimal string (sub-penny safe, e.g. "0.0000024" = 0.0000024 pence per token). Takes precedence over `unit_amount_minor`. Must be > 0 with at most 12 decimal places. Amounts are rounded per tier with half-up (away from zero) before the tier subtotals are summed.

flat_amount_minor.description: Flat fee for entering this tier (minor units). Always a whole number of minor units — only the per-unit RATE supports sub-penny precision.

MeterPriceListResponse.description: A list of prices attached to a meter.

percentage_rate_bps.description: Rate in basis points. 70 = 0.7%. Only meaningful when the price's pricing_model is 'percentage'.

UpdateMeterPriceRequest.description: Parameters for updating a meter price. Active prices on existing subscriptions are not retroactively changed.

precise_amount_minor.description: Unrounded amount in minor units as a decimal string (REV-6211). Not integer cents; sub-penny rates stay exact. Null means not computable for this pricing scheme; never coerce to 0.

OrderListResponse.description: A paginated list of orders matching the query filters.

status.description: Order status. draft: Being built. pending: Awaiting payment. paid: Fully paid. partially_paid: Partial payment received. refunded: Refunded. canceled: Canceled. fulfilled: Shipped/delivered.

billing_type.description: Billing type. one_time: Single purchase. recurring: Subscription-based.

invoice_id.description: ID of the linked invoice (Commercial Truth)

subscription_id.description: ID of the linked subscription (for recurring fulfillment)

Order.description: An order represents a one-off purchase, created when a checkout is fulfilled, with lifecycle operations: update, cancel, and fulfill.

fulfillment_status.description: Fulfilment state of this line; processing means partly shipped

fulfilled_quantity.description: Units of this line shipped so far

OrderLineItem.description: A line item within an order, representing a product, quantity, and unit price.

OrderErrorResponse.description: Error response returned when an order operation fails.

UpdateOrderRequest.description: Parameters for updating order metadata or notes before fulfillment.

CancelOrderRequest.description: Parameters for canceling an order before fulfillment.

line_item_ids.description: Specific line items to fulfill, each in full (defaults to every unfulfilled line)

status.description: Mark the lines shipped (default) or delivered

FulfillOrderRequest.description: Parameters for marking an order as fulfilled, with optional tracking and shipping details.

PaymentListResponse.description: A paginated list of payments matching the query filters.

status.description: Payment status. pending: Processing. authorized: Funds reserved. captured/succeeded: Funds collected. failed: Payment failed. voided: Canceled before capture. refunded/partially_refunded: Returned to customer.

amount_captured.description: Amount captured in cents (for auth-capture flow)

gateway.description: Name of the payment processor that handled this payment

gateway_response_code.description: Normalized response code from the processor

gateway_response_text.description: Human-readable response message from the processor

payment_channel.description: Payment channel. card_present: terminal/POS payment. card_not_present: online or recurring payment. bank_transfer: ACH/direct debit. manual: manually recorded.

entry_mode.description: Card entry mode for card-present (terminal) payments. null for online payments.

Payment.description: A completed or in-progress money movement. Payments represent funds transferred between a customer and your account across all channels — online, terminal, and recurring.

PaymentErrorResponse.description: Error response returned when a payment operation fails.

amount.description: Amount to capture in cents. Defaults to full authorized amount. Must be <= authorized amount.

CapturePaymentRequest.description: Parameters for capturing a previously authorized payment. Optionally specify a partial capture amount.

CancelPaymentRequest.description: Parameters for voiding a payment before settlement. Include a reason for your records.

code.description: Machine-readable error code for programmatic handling

param.description: The parameter that caused the error

decline_code.description: Card decline code from the payment processor

doc_url.description: URL to documentation about this error

ApiError.description: The standard error response envelope. All API errors follow this structure with a machine-readable type and code for programmatic handling, and a human-readable message for debugging.

CreateAccountingInvoicePaymentRequestInp.description: Create an accounting-led invoice payment request and mint/reuse a checkout session.

id.description: Unique identifier for the webhook endpoint

url.description: The URL that receives webhook POST requests

enabled_events.description: Event types this endpoint subscribes to

status.description: Whether the endpoint is currently receiving events

secret.description: Signing secret. Returned only on create or secret rotation.

circuit_breaker_state.description: Circuit breaker status. Opens after repeated delivery failures.

last_delivery_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent delivery attempt

updated_at.description: When the endpoint was last modified

event_id.description: The event this delivery attempted to send.

last_status_code.description: HTTP status code returned on the last attempt.

last_error.description: Truncated error message from the last failed attempt.

customer_id.description: UUID of the customer this session will authenticate as.

ttl_minutes.description: Lifetime of the session token in minutes. Between 5 and 240; default 60. Shorter TTLs reduce blast radius if a token leaks.

CreateCustomerPortalSessionRequest.description: Parameters for creating a customer-portal session. The authenticated merchant must already own the referenced customer.

PortalCustomer.description: The authenticated customer, as visible through the customer-portal surface. This is a deliberately thinner projection than the merchant-facing `Customer` — it omits tax IDs, internal metadata, and anything that could leak merchant-side context to the customer.

PortalSubscription.description: A customer-facing subscription projection. Pricing and cadence fields are exposed; merchant-only bookkeeping fields (plan_id, external IDs) are not.

cancel_at_period_end.description: If `true` (default), cancel at the end of the current period. If `false`, cancel immediately.

reason.description: Merchant-visible note recording why the customer canceled.

PortalInvoice.description: A customer-facing invoice projection. Lists and retrievals are scoped to invoices owned by the authenticated customer.

PortalMandate.description: A customer-facing Direct Debit mandate projection. Bank details are masked — only the last 4 digits of the account number are exposed.

has_more.description: Customer-meter list responses are not paginated — every meter the merchant has is returned for the specified customer.

meter_event_name.description: The `event_name` the merchant's code posts to /v2/usage-events for this meter.

aggregation.description: How quantities are aggregated. Typical values: `sum`, `count`, `max`, `unique`.

total_quantity.description: Aggregate across all usage events for this (customer, meter) pair. The aggregation function applied matches the meter's `aggregation` field.

event_count.description: Number of `usage_events` rows that contributed to the aggregate. Diagnostic — not the aggregate itself.

last_event_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent usage event. Null if no events have been recorded.

CustomerMeter.description: An on-the-fly aggregate of a customer's consumption for a single meter. RevKeen computes this live from `usage_events` — there is no separate `customer_meters` table to keep in sync.

amount_capturable.description: Amount that can be captured (for manual capture)

capture_method.description: Capture method. automatic: Capture immediately on confirmation. manual: Authorize then capture separately.

statement_descriptor.description: Statement descriptor shown on customer's statement

gateway_merchant_id.description: Specific gateway merchant ID for multi-MID setups (NMI)

url.description: The URL for accessing this list

return_url.description: URL to redirect to after 3DS authentication

payment_method_id.description: ID of the payment method to confirm with

return_url.description: URL to redirect to after 3DS authentication

url.description: The URL for accessing this list

EventListResponse.description: A paginated list of events matching the query filters.

coupon.description: Coupon code to apply during this phase

TerminalPaymentResponse.description: A single terminal payment object with full device and transaction details.

invoice_id.description: Associated invoice ID, or null for walk-in/ad-hoc payments

device_id.description: The terminal device that processed (or is processing) this payment

type.description: Transaction type. sale: original charge. refund: money returned. void: pre-settlement cancellation.

status.description: Payment lifecycle status. requested: command sent, awaiting card. in_progress: terminal processing. approved: payment succeeded. declined: issuer declined. cancelled: merchant cancelled. error: terminal error. timed_out: no response within 3 minutes.

amount_minor.description: Amount in minor units (e.g., pence for GBP, cents for USD)

reference.description: Payment reference (invoice number or custom reference)

terminal_serial.description: Serial number of the PAX terminal that processed this payment

uti.description: Unique Transaction Identifier from the terminal

auth_code.description: Authorization code from the payment processor. Present when approved.

rrn.description: Retrieval Reference Number for settlement reconciliation

masked_pan.description: Masked card number — only the last 4 digits are visible

error_message.description: Human-readable error message when status is error or timed_out

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the payment was initiated

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the terminal returned a result, or null if still in progress

TerminalPayment.description: A card-present payment processed through a POS terminal, with device details and card entry mode.

TerminalPaymentErrorResponse.description: Error response returned when a terminal payment operation fails.

device_id.description: The ID of the terminal device to send the payment to. Use List Devices to discover available device IDs. Even merchants with a single terminal must pass the device_id explicitly — there is no auto-routing fallback.

amount_minor.description: Amount in minor units (e.g., pence for GBP, cents for USD)

invoice_id.description: The invoice to charge. Omit for walk-in or ad-hoc payments where no invoice exists. When omitted, the terminal payment is recorded without an invoice association.

reference.description: Custom reference for the payment. Auto-generated if not provided.

CreateTerminalPaymentRequest.description: Parameters for initiating a card-present payment on a POS terminal device.

TerminalPaymentListResponse.description: A paginated list of terminal payments matching the query filters.

invoice_line_item_id.description: An invoice line of the refunded payment

quantity.description: Units of that line to put back on sale

restock_line_items.description: Units to put back on sale once the refund is approved, by invoice line. Omit to restock nothing.

RefundTerminalPaymentRequest.description: Parameters for refunding a completed terminal payment, optionally specifying a partial amount.

VoidTerminalPaymentRequest.description: Parameters for voiding an unsettled terminal payment before end-of-day settlement.

device_name.description: Friendly name assigned to this device (e.g., 'Front Desk Terminal')

terminal_serial.description: Serial number of the paired PAX terminal hardware

platform.description: Operating system of the machine running the Terminal Connector application

terminal_reachable.description: Whether the connector can currently reach the PAX terminal on the local network

app_version.description: Version of the Terminal Connector application

last_heartbeat_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last heartbeat received from this device. Devices with no heartbeat in 5 minutes are considered offline.

TerminalDevice.description: A POS terminal device registered to your merchant account, with connection status and capabilities.

TerminalDeviceErrorResponse.description: Error response returned when a terminal device operation fails.

TerminalDeviceResponse.description: A single terminal device with connection status and configuration details.

UsageEventError.description: Error response returned when a usage event operation fails.

UsageIngestRequest.description: Usage event ingest request. Send either one usage event object directly, or wrap up to 1000 events in an events array.

name.description: Event name matching a meter's event_name

customer_id.description: RevKeen customer ID. Prefer external_customer_id unless your system already stores RevKeen customer UUIDs.

external_customer_id.description: Your external customer identifier. Recommended attribution field; unknown values fail rather than creating orphan usage.

meter_id.description: Direct meter ID (alternative to event name matching)

quantity.description: Event quantity (default: 1). For percentage-priced meters, send the signed transaction amount in the subscription currency's minor units.

metadata.description: Arbitrary properties for filtering and aggregation

UsageEvent.description: A single usage event representing customer consumption of a metered resource. Provide one of customer_id, external_customer_id, or subscription_id. Idempotency is permanent per merchant via the usage_events merchant/idempotency unique index. Each subscription has one currency; usage events attributed to it are interpreted in that currency with no metering-layer FX conversion.

BatchIngestRequest.description: A batch of usage events to ingest, supporting up to 1000 events per request.

DryRunResult.description: Result of a dry-run ingest showing how events would be matched to meters without persisting them.

UsageEventListResponse.description: A paginated list of usage events matching the query filters.

event_name.description: Event name that matched the meter

properties.description: Arbitrary event properties used for filtering/aggregation

UsageAggregateResponse.description: Aggregated usage totals grouped by meter and time period.

total_cost_minor.description: Total cost across all meters (null if no cost data)

percentage_rate_bps.description: Percentage rate in basis points when billing_scheme is percentage. 70 = 0.7%.

**Required Scopes:**

tags.name: Mandates

tags.name: Disputes

Dispute objects represent a customer's challenge to a charge with their card issuer (a chargeback). When a dispute is opened, you can submit evidence to contest it or accept the dispute. RevKeen tracks the dispute lifecycle and notifies you via webhooks at each stage.

tags.name: Events

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Receive real-time event notifications. Configure endpoints for payment events, invoice updates, and more.

## Signature Verification

All webhooks include a signature in the `X-Revkeen-Signature` header for verification:

```
X-Revkeen-Signature: t=1705689600,v1=abc123...
```

**Node.js Example:**
```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');

function verifyWebhook(payload, signature, secret) {
  const [timestamp, hash] = signature.split(',').map(s => s.split('=')[1]);
  const expectedHash = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', secret)
    .update(`${timestamp}.${payload}`)
    .digest('hex');
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(hash), Buffer.from(expectedHash));
}
```

## Event Types

Events use dot notation: `{resource}.{action}`
- `payment.succeeded`, `payment.failed`
- `invoice.created`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.overdue`
- `subscription.created`, `subscription.canceled`, `subscription.renewed`
- `customer.created`, `customer.updated`
- `checkout.session.completed`, `checkout.session.expired`
- `usage.threshold.reached`, `usage.period_finalized`, `usage.invoice.created`, `usage.event.ingested`, `usage.event.rejected`, `usage.event.excluded`, `usage.event.quarantined`, `usage.cap.exceeded`
- `meter.created`, `meter.updated`, `meter.archived`
- `meter_price.created`, `meter_price.updated`, `meter_price.deactivated`

Use wildcards in endpoint configuration: `invoice.*` or `*` for all events.

tags.name: Webhook Endpoints
tags.description: Webhook endpoint objects let you register URLs that RevKeen will notify when events occur in your account — payments, subscription changes, invoice updates, and more. Each endpoint can subscribe to specific event types or use wildcards to receive all events.

tags.name: Webhook Deliveries
tags.description: Individual webhook delivery attempts. Each record represents one attempt chain to one endpoint for one event, capturing the HTTP status code, error, duration, and retry schedule. Use these to debug a specific failed delivery (for example, a 503 from a staging endpoint) and to queue an immediate retry. This is the grain Stripe and Polar expose for webhook debugging — use `/v2/events/:id/resend` when you want to re-dispatch the event across **all** endpoints instead.

tags.name: Customer Portal
tags.description:
A programmatic customer-portal surface. Mint a short-lived bearer token via `POST /v2/customer-portal/sessions` for a specific customer, then hand that token to the customer's browser or to an app acting on their behalf. Subsequent `/v2/customer-portal/*` calls authenticate as that customer — returning only that customer's own subscriptions and invoices, and letting them self-cancel a subscription.

This is distinct from the hosted customer portal (cookie-based, rendered by RevKeen). Use the hosted portal when you want a drop-in self-service page; use the programmatic surface here when you're embedding self-service inside your own app with your own UI.

Tokens are Polar-shaped: prefix `rkcps_`, 60-minute default TTL, no server-side revocation list in v1 (short TTL and re-mint are the revocation story).

tags.name: Customer Meters
tags.description:
Per-customer usage aggregates, computed live from `usage_events`. Given a customer, return the total consumption per meter the merchant has defined. Use this to power "current usage" UI inside embedded portals — Polar exposes the same primitive and it's the shape billing-savvy agents expect.

RevKeen does not maintain a separate `customer_meters` table. Aggregates are derived on demand from `usage_events` grouped by `(customer_id, meter_id)`. This keeps the write path cheap and always up-to-date; there is no batch to fall behind.

The path uses a composite ID `(customer_id, meter_id)` rather than a synthetic single-segment ID because both components are first-class entities the caller already holds.

tags.name: Terminal Payments

Initiate and manage card-present payments via POS terminal devices. Send sale, refund, and void commands to PAX terminals through the RevKeen connector.

- `terminal:write` - Initiate, cancel, refund, void terminal payments

**MCP Tools:** `terminal_payments_initiate`, `terminal_payments_list`, `terminal_payments_get`, `terminal_payments_cancel`, `terminal_payments_refund`, `terminal_payments_void`

tags.name: Terminal Devices
tags.description:
List and inspect terminal devices registered for your merchant account. Use this endpoint to discover device IDs before initiating terminal payments.

**Required Scopes:**
- `terminal:read` - List and retrieve terminal devices

**MCP Tools:** `terminal_devices_list`, `terminal_devices_get`

tags.name: Payment Attempts
tags.description: Track payment attempts across all gateways. Analyze retry patterns and failure reasons.

tags.name: External Sync

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description: Manage external integrations (PracticeHub, Wodify). List active integrations and update status.

tags.name: Sync State
tags.description: Track sync progress for external integrations. Get and update sync state by resource type.

- `integrations:write` - Create accounting-led invoice payment requests

tags.name: Meters
tags.description:
Create and manage usage meters. Meters define how usage events are aggregated for billing. Attach prices to meters for automated usage-based invoicing.

- `prices:write` - Create, update, archive meters and prices

tags.name: Invoice Line Items
tags.description:
Invoice line item utilities. Includes usage provenance: trace a usage line back to the billing entries, meter matches, and events that produced it.

**Required Scopes:**
- `invoices:read`

tags.name: Usage Events

tags.name: Usage

Query current-period usage balance with estimated costs per meter. Includes included allowance, overage, and margin data.

**Required Scopes:**
- `usage:read` - Get usage balance

**MCP Tools:** `usage_balance_get`

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description:
Revenue analytics including MRR summaries, time-series data, accounts receivable aging, days sales outstanding (DSO), and customer lifetime value (LTV). Use these endpoints to build dashboards and financial reports.

**Required Scopes:**
- `analytics:read` - Access analytics endpoints

tags.name: Finance

Financial summaries and income reports. Get a high-level overview of your business finances including revenue, expenses, and net income.

- `finance:read` - Access finance endpoints

tags.name: Transactions

tags.name: Imports

tags.name: Exports

**Required Scopes:**
- `exports:read` - Check export status
- `exports:write` - Create export jobs

post.summary: Convert a cart session into a checkout session
post.description:
Atomically materialise a pending checkout session from the cart snapshot, reserve tracked availability, flip the cart to `converted`, and emit `commerce.cart.converted` + `commerce.checkout.started` through the outbox.

Idempotent on re-call (returns the existing checkout session). Concurrency-safe via a compare-and-swap lock on cart status; product availability is guarded by the database reserve step.

Validation that runs inside the lock and rolls back on failure:
- `CART_SESSION_EMPTY` — the cart has no line items.
- `AVAILABILITY_EXCEEDED` — a tracked/capacity-limited product can no longer satisfy the requested quantity.
- `CART_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` — no cart for this id under the calling merchant.
- `CART_SESSION_CLOSED` — the cart is already `abandoned` or `expired`.

On rollback the cart returns to `open` and the customer can retry after fixing the cause.

post.description:
Create a new subscription for a customer.

**The first period is billed at creation**, at the price's amount for the quantity. On card the saved `paymentMethodId` is charged straight away (it is required unless the subscription starts in a trial). On Direct Debit the first collection is scheduled with advance notice, typically 5–7 working days after creation. With a trial, nothing is billed until the trial ends.

Set `paymentRail: direct_debit` with an active `mandateId` to create a Direct Debit subscription (GBP only). This needs a signed-in team member or an OAuth app; API keys are refused with 403.

- `POST /subscriptions/{id}/change-plan` — Change subscription plan
- `POST /subscriptions/{id}/change-quantity` — Change subscription quantity

- `403 authorization_error` — the caller is identified but the action is denied. Codes include `insufficient_permissions`, `ip_not_allowed`, `merchant_mismatch`, and `origin_not_allowed`.
- `404 resource_missing` — the referenced resource does not exist or is not visible to your key.
- `422 unprocessable_entity` — business-rule failure (for example, refunding more than the original charge).

currency.description: Not used: a payment link takes its currency from its products. For an ad-hoc line item, set line_items[].price_data.currency.

invoice_id.description: Deprecated and ignored. This endpoint does not create a payment link for an invoice.

success_url.description: Custom URL to redirect after successful payment. Supports placeholders: {CHECKOUT_ID}, {TRANSACTION_ID}, {PAYMENT_ID}, {CUSTOMER_ID}, {AMOUNT}, {CURRENCY}, {PORTAL_URL}, {CHECKOUT_STATUS_TOKEN}. If not set, redirects to RevKeen's default success page.

cancel_url.description: Custom URL to redirect if customer cancels the checkout. If not set, no cancel redirect is configured.

collect_shipping.description: When true, checkout asks the customer for a delivery address before payment.

allow_promotion_codes.description: Not applied yet: links created through this endpoint do not accept discount codes, whatever this is set to.

tax_behavior.description: Whether the link's prices include tax. inclusive or exclusive is saved on the link; unspecified keeps the default (exclusive). Tax is only calculated when the link's tax mode is manual or auto, which this endpoint does not set.

post.description:
Send usage events for billing. Accepts a single event or a batch of up to 1000 events.

**Single event:** Send the event object directly in the request body.
**Batch:** Wrap events in an `events` array.

Events are matched to meters by `name` (event name) or `meter_id`. At least one of `customer_id`, `external_customer_id`, or `subscription_id` is required.

**Idempotency:** provide `idempotency_key` per event. The key is unique per merchant forever; repeats return `duplicate` and do not create another billable event.

**Attribution:** prefer `external_customer_id` when your system owns customer identifiers. Unknown external IDs fail fast instead of creating orphan usage.

**Currency:** each subscription has one currency. Usage attributed to that subscription is interpreted in that currency; RevKeen does not perform FX conversion in the metering layer.

---

**Related endpoints**

- `GET /usage-events` — Query usage events
- `POST /usage-events/dry-run` — Dry-run usage events
- `GET /usage-events/aggregate/{meterId}` — Get aggregated usage
- `GET /usage-events/{id}` — Get a usage event

**Common errors**

- `400 invalid_request` — malformed payload or failed validation.
- `401 authentication_error` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credential. Codes: `authentication_failed`, `invalid_api_key`, `expired_api_key`, `api_key_revoked`, `session_invalid`, `merchant_required`. Carries a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge.

**Idempotency**

Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header (UUID v4 recommended) to make retries safe. Keys are valid for 24 hours; see [the idempotency guide](/docs/fundamentals/idempotency).

post.summary: Schedule a one-off Direct Debit collection
post.description:
Schedules a one-off Bacs collection against an active mandate for an invoice or payment link. L&Z confirms the permitted collection date, the payer receives the configured regulatory advance notice first, and nothing is marked paid until the bureau confirms collection. Idempotent per source: retrying with the same sourceId returns or reconciles the same provider schedule instead of collecting twice. An invoice source must be issued and still owe money: a draft or pending_approval invoice is refused, and so are paid, void and other closed invoices (409 invoice_not_collectable at the final check before bureau submission).
